Note::from_latin1¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::from_latin1() const

Decode Latin-1 Bytes Into UTF-8 Text¶

from_latin1() reads each cell’s bytes as ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1) — where every byte value 0x00–0xFF is the code point with that same number — and returns a UTF-8 text-mode Note holding the decoded characters. Reach for it when a bytes-mode Note came from a legacy file, protocol, or database column that stores Western-European text as one byte per character.

Latin-1 has no undefined byte values, so the decode never fails and never substitutes: every input byte becomes exactly one Unicode scalar, and the character count of the result equals the byte length of the input. Byte 0xE9 becomes é (U+00E9), 0xA9 becomes © (U+00A9), and the ASCII range 0x00–0x7F is unchanged.

The operation is shape-preserving and cell-independent. The result is tagged UTF-8 text regardless of the input mode; calling it on a Note that is already text re-interprets that text’s bytes as Latin-1, which is only meaningful if the text was mis-tagged. The inverse is to_latin1_lossy; for the Windows superset that maps 0x80–0x9F to smart quotes, dashes, and the euro sign, use from_windows1252.

Example 1: High Bytes Become Their Latin-1 Characters¶

const pluss::Note raw = pluss::note::bytes({std::string("caf") + '\xE9' + " " + '\xA9'});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(raw.from_latin1()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["café ©"]

0xE9 → é, 0xA9 → ©; the result is UTF-8 text.

Example 2: Round Trip Through to_latin1_lossy¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({std::string("caf") + "é"})
                 .to_latin1_lossy()
                 .from_latin1()
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"café"

Any text whose characters are all U+0000–U+00FF survives to_latin1_lossy().from_latin1() unchanged.

See Also¶

  • Note::to_latin1_lossy: the inverse — UTF-8 text back to Latin-1 bytes.

  • Note::from_windows1252: the Windows-1252 superset of Latin-1.

  • Note::to_utf8_strict / Note::to_utf8_lossy: promote bytes that are already UTF-8 to text mode.
